frequency_question: How often does institutional or legal friction prevent the operationalization of a mandated liquidity absorption tool once the central bank initiates the policy pathway?
membership_rule: Includes any formal announcement or consideration of reserve-ratio adjustments or incremental liquidity management instruments by major emerging market central banks where banking sector pushback or operational friction is documented; excludes general monetary policy rate adjustments.

cases.name: People's Bank of China Reserve Requirement Ratio Adjustments
Bank Indonesia Secondary Reserve Requirement Implementation
Central Bank of Brazil Compulsory Deposit Rule Adjustments
South African Reserve Bank Cash Reserve Requirement Shifts

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named prominent historical occurrences; comprehensive of major liquidity-absorption tool usages where institutional friction was a reported variable.
known_gaps: Excludes minor unannounced back-channel adjustments or failed internal proposals that did not reach the threshold of public institutional friction testing.
skeleton: Central bank regulatory interventions meeting statutory authority criteria across high-capacity emerging markets
multiplier: 6 observed implementations / 6 attempts where administrative friction was tested
validity_reason: Central bank statutory powers and institutional independence frameworks remain stable over medium-term horizons unless legislative overhauls occur.
